memos.summary:
### Bottom line

- A [quarter-point hike](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXFEDDECISION) to 4.00–4.25% is very likely December 9. [November CPI](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/12_sched.htm?view=full) arrives December 10: it can tip January’s close call, not December’s decision.
- Cheaper [gasoline](https://gasprices.aaa.com/gas-prices-keep-dropping-as-thanksgiving-approaches/) could lower headline CPI even as [core prices](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXCPICORE) rise. For retailers, this week’s possible [tariff proposals](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/privacy-and-data-security/us-readies-tariff-hike-on-china-eu-goods-as-soon-as-tuesday) matter most for which goods face duties and when.
- A [U.S.–Iran ceasefire](https://polymarket.com/event/us-x-iran-effective-ceasefire-by-november-30-20261108) is likely by November 30; [normal Hormuz traffic](https://polymarket.com/event/strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to-normal-by-december-31) is unlikely by year-end. Until fuel exports recover, [scarce diesel](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-november-2026) favors Valero and squeezes truckers.
- Dell is widely expected to clear [$35 billion](https://polymarket.com/event/will-dell-q3-infrastructure-solutions-group-revenue-be-above-35pt0b) in quarterly infrastructure sales. With [memory costs](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/_assets/_62d48350371e13cf7ba6bdf1e3ae1212/delltechnologies/db/3595/34748/webcast_transcript/Q2_FY27_Transcript.pdf) rising, margins matter more than a revenue beat.

### Themes

**Rates and housing**
- November [payrolls](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXPAYROLLS) near 90,000 and [Q4 growth](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXGDP) near 3% annualized suggest slower hiring, not recession. If inflation cools, lower [mortgage rates](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms/pmms_archives) help homebuilders. If hiring breaks, favor long Treasuries over builders.
- If retailers [pass duties through](https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/staff_reports/sr1201), broader price increases favor inflation-protected Treasuries over comparable nominal bonds.

**AI hardware**
- Higher [memory prices](https://investors.micron.com/static-files/23023765-dfef-4e7e-845b-cd744fc20d93) benefit Micron. Dell and HPE can raise revenue without shipping more servers if customers accept price increases.
- A tariff extension would not undo [chip export controls](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-11-19/pdf/2026-23529.pdf). [Nvidia’s forecast](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/default.aspx) excludes China data-center compute sales; continued restrictions cap upside.

**Bitcoin exposure**
- A [sub-$55,000 dip](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXBTCMINY) is more likely than not, even if Bitcoin [finishes higher](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXBTCY) at $55,000–$65,000. [Strategy sold Bitcoin](https://www.strategy.com/press/strategy-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-results_10-29-2026) to fund preferred dividends and buybacks—a financing risk spot holders avoid.

### Dates to watch

- **Nov. 24:** [Dell call](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/), 4:30 p.m. ET—server pricing and margins.
- **Nov. 25:** [October PCE](https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule/full) and revised Q3 GDP test inflation and demand.
- **Nov. 29:** [OPEC+ meets](https://www.opec.org/pr-detail/605-7-june-2026.html); quotas matter less if [tankers cannot sail](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/report/global_oil.php).
- **Dec. 3:** [Huang testifies](https://www.banking.senate.gov/hearings/protecting-americas-ai-advantage-oversight-of-us-export-controls) on chip export controls.
- **Dec. 4:** [November jobs report](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/home.htm) tests the hiring slowdown.
- **Dec. 9–10:** [Fed projections](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm) precede [November CPI](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/12_sched.htm?view=full).
- **Dec. 11:** [Federal funding expires](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2026.09.28-Apportionment-of-the-Continuing-Resolutions-for-Fiscal-Year-2027-1.pdf). Even a stopgap can [delay defense contracts](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-26-107065).

### Bottom line

- Bitcoin is more likely than not to [dip below $55,000](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXBTCMINY) by December 31, yet its two leading [year-end ranges](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXBTCY) span $55,000–$65,000. A selloff and a partial recovery are compatible.
- On November 23, investors withdrew $570 million from [Bitcoin ETFs](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/) and $85 million from [Ether ETFs](https://farside.co.uk/ethereum-etf-flow-all-data/). Sustained inflows would strengthen the rebound case more than another fund launch. ([farside.co.uk](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/))

### What is priced in

- By December 31, an [Ether dip](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXETHMINY) below $1,500 is slightly favored; [Solana below $60](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXSOLMINY) and a [$2 trillion](https://polymarket.com/event/will-total-crypto-market-cap-dip-to-2t-in-2026-20260721192934670) total crypto valuation are each roughly a coin toss.
- XRP signals conflict: the [$4.25–$4.50 close](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXXRPY) draws strong support even though [exceeding $4](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXXRPMAXY) during 2026 is a long shot. The high closing range is a poor base case.
- Neither a [Bitcoin record](https://polymarket.com/event/bitcoin-all-time-high-by-december-31-2026) nor [CLARITY Act passage](https://polymarket.com/event/clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026) is expected this year.

### Second-order effects

- **MARA:** At $50,000 Bitcoin, roughly $10,300 per coin would remain before other costs, using its third-quarter owned-site [power cost](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000150760526000026/q326shareholderletter.htm). A rebound widens that margin. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000150760526000026/q326shareholderletter.htm))
- **Strategy:** A prolonged decline could prompt more Bitcoin sales. By October 29, Strategy had already [sold $432 million](https://www.strategy.com/press/strategy-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-results_10-29-2026) of Bitcoin to help fund preferred dividends and buybacks. Common shareholders bear that financing risk; spot holders do not. ([strategy.com](https://www.strategy.com/press/strategy-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-results_10-29-2026?utm_source=openai))
- **Coinbase and Circle:** Heavy selling can generate [trading fees](https://investor.coinbase.com/files/content_files/Q3_26-Earnings-Deck.pdf) for Coinbase. Binance says it [replaced stolen assets](https://www.binance.com/en/blog/community/2389609752772696140); U.S. prosecutors are separately [seeking forfeiture](https://www.justice.gov/usao-dc/media/1473936/dl?inline=) of frozen USDC. For Circle’s earnings, lower rates are the clearer risk: third-quarter [reserve income](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1876042/000187604226000309/finalq3epr-110326.htm) fell despite higher average USDC circulation. ([investor.coinbase.com](https://investor.coinbase.com/files/content_files/Q3_26-Earnings-Deck.pdf))

### Dates to watch

- **November 30:** Ether [below $1,500](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXETHMINMON) remains possible but unlikely this month.
- **December 9:** [Fed rate decision](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2026-december.htm) matters for stablecoin earnings. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2026-december.htm?utm_source=openai))
- **December 10:** [SEC comments](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/self-regulatory-organization-rulemaking/sr-cboebzx-2026-093) close on listing-rule changes for Invesco’s existing Bitcoin and Ether ETFs—not new fund approvals. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/self-regulatory-organization-rulemaking/sr-cboebzx-2026-093?utm_source=openai))

### Bottom line

- A [quarter-point hike](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXFEDDECISION) to 4.00–4.25% on December 9 is very likely. January and March are each close calls between another hike and a hold; by April, a pause is favored.
- November CPI arrives **after** the December decision. For homebuilders and long-duration Treasuries, the bigger risk is whether that report makes a January hike more likely. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm))

### What is priced in

- October [core PCE](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXPCECORE) likely rose 0.3% monthly, taking annual inflation from September’s 3.1% to 3.2–3.3%. November headline CPI could fall 0.1% even as [core prices](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXCPICORE) rise 0.2–0.3%. That split argues against treating cheaper energy as broad disinflation. ([bea.gov](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-september-2026))
- November [payrolls](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXPAYROLLS) center near 90,000, down from October’s 165,000, with unemployment near 4.1–4.2%. [Q4 growth](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXGDP) near 3% annualized after 3.4% in Q3 suggests slower hiring, not recession. ([bls.gov](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_11062026.htm?utm_source=openai))
- The Fed held in October, but almost all officials expected further tightening. On November 23, New York Fed President [John Williams](https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/speeches/2026/wil261123) still saw resilient demand and persistent inflation. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20261028.htm))

### Second-order effects

- **Hot core inflation and firm hiring:** Extra hikes could push two-year yields up faster than ten-year yields, narrowing November 23’s 29-basis-point spread. A wider U.S. rate advantage would support the dollar, though expected [ECB tightening](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXCBDECISIONEU) limits the case against the euro. ([home.treasury.gov](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?field_tdr_date_value=2026&trk=public_post_comment-text&type=daily_treasury_yield_curve))
- **Cooling inflation, steady employment:** Falling long yields would lift long-duration Treasuries and ease mortgage costs from [7.28%](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms/pmms_archives), helping homebuilders. If yields fall because hiring breaks instead, favor Treasuries over builders: cheaper mortgages cannot replace lost paychecks. ([investor.gov](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-86?utm_source=openai))

### Dates to watch

- **Nov 25:** [October PCE](https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule/full) and revised Q3 GDP. ([bea.gov](https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule/full?utm_source=openai))
- **Dec 4:** [November payrolls](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/home.htm) and unemployment. ([bls.gov](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/home.htm?utm_source=openai))
- **Dec 9:** [Fed decision](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm) and updated rate projections. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm))
- **Dec 10:** [November CPI](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/12_sched.htm?view=full), the first inflation test for January. ([bls.gov](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/12_sched.htm?view=full&utm_source=openai))

### Bottom line

- **Diesel and jet fuel matter more than $100 crude.** Falling gasoline helps households, but scarce refined fuels support Valero’s margins and squeeze truckers and airlines. ([gasprices.aaa.com](https://gasprices.aaa.com/gas-prices-keep-dropping-as-thanksgiving-approaches/?utm_source=openai))
- **Hormuz matters more than an OPEC+ quota increase** if tankers cannot move the extra barrels. Restored shipping would favor fuel buyers over U.S. oil producers. ([eia.gov](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/report/global_oil.php))

### What is priced in

- WTI touching [$100](https://polymarket.com/event/will-wti-reach-100-in-november-2026-from-november-2) by November 30 is a long shot; [year-end WTI](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXWTIDIRY) above $80 is a coin toss. More than 15 [Hormuz transits](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXHORMUZWEEKLY) this week is narrowly favored; more than 20 is unlikely. ([kalshi.com](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxhormuzweekly/traffic-through-the-strait-of-hormuz/kxhormuzweekly-26nov29))
- November 30 favors [gasoline](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXAAAGASM) at $3.50–$3.55 per gallon versus [diesel](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXDIESELMON) at $5.60–$5.70. Gold touching [$3,500](https://polymarket.com/event/will-xauusd-dip-to-3500-in-november-2026) by then is slightly favored; silver could touch both [$40](https://polymarket.com/event/will-xagusd-dip-to-40-in-november-2026) and [$44](https://polymarket.com/event/will-xagusd-reach-44-in-november-2026-from-november-23). ([kalshi.com](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxaaagasm/us-gas-price/kxaaagasm-26nov30?utm_source=openai))

### Second-order effects

- Damaged overseas refineries and winter heating demand keep diesel scarce. Washington [permits Russian diesel](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261009_33), but [November deliveries](https://polymarket.com/event/us-imports-russian-diesel-by-november-30) are unlikely. Cheaper gasoline eases headline inflation before lower freight costs reach store shelves. ([eia.gov](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/report/petro_prod.php?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block&utm_source=openai))
- If Gulf exports recover, crude producers lose pricing power. Airlines need **jet fuel**, not just crude, to get cheaper: United’s quarterly [fuel bill](https://ir.united.com/node/34056/ixbrl-viewer) rose $1.8 billion year over year. ([eia.gov](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/report/global_oil.php))
- A [cold spell](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?format=txt&glossary=1&issuedby=SPD&product=PMD&site=DTX&version=1) could push [PJM Western](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXPJMWESTW) above $60/MWh this week, benefiting generators selling at spot prices. [ERCOT North](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXERCOTNORTHW) is likelier to stay below $30/MWh. ([forecast.weather.gov](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?format=txt&glossary=1&issuedby=SPD&product=PMD&site=DTX&version=1&utm_source=openai))
- Gold-fund [outflows](https://www.gold.org/download/file/21413/WMM-23-Nov-2026-AI-reckoning.pdf) weaken bullion demand. Newmont faces a second squeeze that bullion holders avoid: higher [diesel costs](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1164727/000116472726000041/newmontq32026earningsrelea.htm) even if gold holds steady. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/download/file/21413/WMM-23-Nov-2026-AI-reckoning.pdf))

### Dates to watch

- **Nov. 25:** [PCE inflation](https://www.bea.gov/index.php/news/schedule/) at 8:30 a.m. ET; [crude inventories](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/schedule.php) at 10:30. Roughly [418 million barrels](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXEIACRUDEW) is expected outside the strategic reserve. ([bea.gov](https://www.bea.gov/index.php/news/schedule/?utm_source=openai))
- **Nov. 29:** [OPEC+ ministers](https://www.opec.org/pr-detail/605-7-june-2026.html) meet on production policy; seven members have already held December targets steady. ([opec.org](https://www.opec.org/pr-detail/605-7-june-2026.html?utm_source=openai))
- **Dec. 25:** Whether the [strategic reserve](https://polymarket.com/event/will-us-crude-oil-reserves-fall-to-260m-by-december-25-2026) falls to 260 million barrels remains a coin toss.

Ending the [U.S. blockade](https://polymarket.com/event/us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockade-by-march-31-2027) remains a coin toss even by March 31, 2027.

### Second-order effects

- Qatar is mediating a proposed exchange of [sanctions relief](https://apnews.com/article/vance-rubio-qatar-iran-war-16e0c2cb05347cfcac068ec4aebb363f) for safer passage. Cheaper marine insurance would help restart sailings; renewed attacks could instead lift freight costs and demand for [gold](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-mid-year-outlook-2026). ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/vance-rubio-qatar-iran-war-16e0c2cb05347cfcac068ec4aebb363f))
- The IEA expects a fourth-quarter oil surplus, yet Gulf export losses and Russian refinery attacks keep [diesel scarce](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-november-2026). That favors U.S. refiners such as Valero over crude producers. Restored fuel exports would narrow refining margins and help truckers. ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-november-2026))
- A Ukraine truce need not cut European defense orders: Kyiv’s allies envision continued [military support](https://president.gov.ua/en/news/spilna-zayava-lideriv-nimechchini-franciyi-velikoyi-britaniy-107409). Nor would it automatically reverse Europe’s [Russian gas ban](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/ending-russian-energy-imports/), which supports demand for alternative LNG suppliers. ([president.gov.ua](https://president.gov.ua/en/news/spilna-zayava-lideriv-nimechchini-franciyi-velikoyi-britaniy-107409))
- A U.S.–China tariff extension would protect importers’ margins without necessarily helping Nvidia: separate [export controls](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-11-19/pdf/2026-23529.pdf) restrict Chinese customers’ use of advanced chips abroad. ([uscc.gov](https://www.uscc.gov/sites/default/files/2026-11/Chapter_1--U.S.-China_Economic_and_Trade_Relations_Year_in_Review.pdf?utm_source=openai))

### Dates to watch

- **November 25:** Israeli [action in Lebanon](https://polymarket.com/event/israel-military-action-against-lebanon-on-november-25) is widely expected, not itself a break with Iran.
- **November 30:** [Hormuz transits](https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-between-0-and-4-average-daily-transits-of-the-strait-of-hormuz-on-november-30) test whether diplomacy is moving cargo.
- **December 14–15:** Trump and Xi are expected to meet at the [Miami G20](https://www.miamibeachfl.gov/g20/) before the January tariff-truce expiry. ([miamibeachfl.gov](https://www.miamibeachfl.gov/g20/?utm_source=openai))
- **May–August 2027:** Possible U.S.–China trade and technology talks; new [chipmaking restrictions](https://polymarket.com/event/china-chip-manufacturing-export-restrictions-become-law-by-june-30-2027) are a coin toss by June 30.

### Bottom line

- Israel’s near-term market test is whether a coalition can pass a budget. Gadi Eisenkot is the [favorite](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXISRAELPM) to become prime minister; prolonged caretaker rule is the main alternative. ([kalshi.com](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxisraelpm/who-will-be-the-prime-minister-of-israel-after-their-election/kxisraelpm-26oct27))
- The dollar bought [3.345 shekels](https://www.boi.org.il/en/economic-roles/financial-markets/exchange-rates/) on November 24. A durable coalition could reverse part of the postelection slide, lifting dollar returns on unhedged Israeli bonds. A failed confidence vote would leave both the currency and those returns exposed. ([boi.org.il](https://www.boi.org.il/en/economic-roles/financial-markets/exchange-rates/?utm_source=openai))

### What is priced in

- Benjamin Netanyahu’s [year-end departure](https://polymarket.com/event/netanyahu-out-before-2027-684-719-226-657) is roughly a coin toss; his departure by [March 31](https://polymarket.com/event/netanyahu-out-by-march-31-2027) is favored. He has a slight edge to receive the [second mandate](https://polymarket.com/event/will-benjamin-netanyahu-receive-the-second-mandate-to-form-a-government-after-the-2026-israeli-election-20261105190000000), but another chance to negotiate is not a governing majority. No other named contender comes close to Eisenkot. ([kalshi.com](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxisraelpm/who-will-be-the-prime-minister-of-israel-after-their-election/kxisraelpm-26oct27))

### Second-order effects

- **Eisenkot coalition:** His Yashar party would [ease import barriers](https://yasharwitheisenkot.com/principles/economics/) and redirect tax and housing benefits toward working families and reservists. Import competition would pressure incumbent distributors. A shekel rebound would also raise the dollar cost of Israeli operations for [Intel](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm) and squeeze [Vishay’s margins](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000019/form10k.htm). ([yasharwitheisenkot.com](https://yasharwitheisenkot.com/principles/economics/))
- **Netanyahu coalition:** Likud’s push to buy more munitions domestically favors Elbit Systems over foreign suppliers competing for new orders. Elbit already holds [multiyear contracts](https://www.mod.gov.il/en/press-releases/press-room/israel-mod-procures-over-200m-elbit-systems-aerial-munitions); those do not depend on Netanyahu winning. ([mod.gov.il](https://www.mod.gov.il/en/press-releases/press-room/israel-mod-procures-over-200m-elbit-systems-aerial-munitions?utm_source=openai))
- **No deal:** A [provisional budget](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/rexnr6xcn) would delay new infrastructure projects, hurting contractors. Further shekel weakness would make imports dearer and leave less room for rate cuts, weighing on longer-dated Israeli bonds. ([calcalistech.com](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/rexnr6xcn?utm_source=openai))

### Dates to watch

- **December 6, 2026:** Eisenkot’s [mandate expires](https://israelpolicyforum.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Forming-Israels-Next-Government-Interests-Red-Lines-and-Coalition-Prospects_IPF-Explains-In-Brief.pdf); the president can extend it to December 20. ([israelpolicyforum.org](https://israelpolicyforum.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Forming-Israels-Next-Government-Interests-Red-Lines-and-Coalition-Prospects_IPF-Explains-In-Brief.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **January 1, 2027:** Without an approved budget, [temporary spending limits](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/z3g4nx8j4) would constrain new projects. ([calcalistech.com](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/z3g4nx8j4?utm_source=openai))

- [Nvidia’s forecast](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/default.aspx) assumes no China data-center compute revenue. Tighter licenses would limit a recovery, not directly cut that forecast; resumed shipments would be upside. ([investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

([energy.senate.gov](https://www.energy.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Data-Center-One-Pager.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- Even without a shutdown, a stopgap can delay [new defense contracts](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-26-107065). A lapse could also delay payments for work already done. ([gao.gov](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-26-107065?utm_source=openai))

### Bottom line

- A mild [northern U.S. winter](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/90day/fxus05.html) matters more for gas producers than whether El Niño breaks a record. Lower heating demand favors fertilizer makers that buy gas. ([cpc.ncep.noaa.gov](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/90day/fxus05.html?utm_source=openai))
- Thanksgiving’s [coastal storm](https://origin-east-www-wpc.woc.noaa.gov/discussions/pmdspd.html), not another hurricane, is the immediate threat to East Coast utilities and holiday freight along I-95. ([origin-east-www-wpc.woc.noaa.gov](https://origin-east-www-wpc.woc.noaa.gov/discussions/pmdspd.html))

### What is priced in

- Global heat records are very likely for [November](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXHMONTH) and [2026](https://kalshi.com/markets/KXGTEMP). A [record El Niño](https://polymarket.com/event/will-the-2026-27-el-nino-be-the-strongest-on-record) is favored over the full season; reaching +2.5°C on the relative Pacific temperature index in November–January is closer to a coin toss. NOAA leans toward crossing it. ([berkeleyearth.org](https://berkeleyearth.org/october-2026-temperature-update/))
- [Isaias](https://www.noaa.gov/news-release/hurricane-season-wrap-up-el-nino-fueled-record-number-of-pacific-storms-but-calmed-atlantic) will likely remain the only major Atlantic hurricane. It peaked at Category 3 but hit Florida at Category 2; a U.S. Category 4 landfall is remote. ([noaa.gov](https://www.noaa.gov/news-release/hurricane-season-wrap-up-el-nino-fueled-record-number-of-pacific-storms-but-calmed-atlantic))
- A [new pandemic](https://polymarket.com/event/new-pandemic-before-2028) remains unlikely through 2027. Congo’s Ebola outbreak is an international emergency, not a pandemic. CDC confirmed [four dairy-worker infections](https://www.cdc.gov/bird-flu/spotlights/bird-flu-update-11232026.html) with H5 in Washington and Oregon, without detected person-to-person spread. ([who.int](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON630?utm_source=openai))

### Second-order effects

- EIA cut its [winter gas forecast](https://www.eia.gov/pressroom/releases/press594.php) to $2.87 per million Btu. Sustained cold would favor gas producers and erode CF Industries’ fertilizer cost advantage. ([eia.gov](https://www.eia.gov/pressroom/releases/press594.php?utm_source=openai))
- A quiet Atlantic limits wind claims now, but cheaper January reinsurance helps property insurers buying protection and pressures sellers. [RenaissanceRe](https://investor.renre.com/reports-filings/sec-filings/content/0000913144-26-000098/rnr-20260930.htm) already reports lower property premiums from rate cuts. ([ajg.com](https://www.ajg.com/gallagherre/-/media/files/gallagher/gallagherre/2026/gallagher-re-first-view-july-2026-a-moment-for-creativity.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- Storm repairs hit utility cash flow before earnings: [Florida Power & Light](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/37634/000075330826000081/R24.htm) can recover eligible costs later through customer surcharges. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/37634/000075330826000081/R24.htm?utm_source=openai))
- El Niño need not lift food inflation. USDA raised [wheat output forecasts](https://ers.usda.gov/media/30362/whs-26k.pdf) for Australia and Argentina and lowered its wholesale egg-price forecast, easing cost pressure for bakers. ([ers.usda.gov](https://ers.usda.gov/media/30362/whs-26k.pdf))

### Dates to watch

- **Nov. 25–26:** [Coastal flooding](https://origin-east-www-wpc.woc.noaa.gov/discussions/pmdspd.html) threatens Georgia through the Northeast. ([origin-east-www-wpc.woc.noaa.gov](https://origin-east-www-wpc.woc.noaa.gov/discussions/pmdspd.html))

- **Jan. 1, 2027:** [Reinsurance renewals](https://www.ajg.com/gallagherre/-/media/files/gallagher/gallagherre/2026/gallagher-re-first-view-july-2026-a-moment-for-creativity.pdf) test pricing.
